title: Orange Rotors Overnight Do Not Automatically Mean Ruined Rotors
topic: Light brake-rotor surface oxidation after moisture is not automatically replacement
mechanicTruth: Exposed iron brake rotors can develop light surface oxidation after moisture; light oxidation may clear from the swept surface during normal braking, while persistent corrosion, pitting, noise, pulsation, or degraded braking calls for inspection.

voiceoverScript: Brake rotors can turn orange quickly after sitting wet. Light surface oxidation does not automatically mean replacement. What matters is whether it clears normally and whether corrosion, noise, pulsation, or braking behavior persists.
selectedCaption: Orange rotor color after a wet night is not an automatic brake-job verdict. Light surface oxidation and persistent corrosion are different conditions.
